components.gap: Not every claimed theorem of Barwise ch. A.1 pp. 5-46 is supplied with its exact hypotheses and a complete source proof route. (1) 5.7 for general languages (handbook/parts/p02/propositional-languages-valuations-and-truth-functions-w02c-p02-003.tex:115-166, handbook/annex/p02/propositional-languages-valuations-and-truth-functions-w02c-p02-003.tex:71-137) is proved only under the added occurrence and replacement conditions of def:p02-w02c-p02-003-general-reading, which 5.7 does not name; the general-limit warning (handbook/parts/p02/propositional-languages-valuations-and-truth-functions-w02c-p02-003.tex:187-197) leaves the comparison with Barwise [1974] and the case without replacement unsettled. (2) Keisler's Completeness and Compactness Theorems for L(Q) (pp. 44-45) are not proved (def:p02-w02c-p02-003-beyond-boundary, handbook/parts/p02/propositional-languages-valuations-and-truth-functions-w02c-p02-003.tex:867-878). (3) The p. 16 claims are proved only conditionally or not at all (def:p02-w02c-p02-003-theories-boundary, handbook/parts/p02/propositional-languages-valuations-and-truth-functions-w02c-p02-003.tex:1014-1049): decidability of abelian groups (Szmielew) and undecidability of groups are not proved; completeness of ACF_p rests on the cited thm:p03-acfp-uncountable-categorical (Steinitz) with no proof; decidability of ACF_0 and of C is proved only under the unproved hypotheses that an algebraically closed field of characteristic 0 exists and that C is algebraically closed (fundamental theorem of algebra); undecidability of Z is proved only under Lagrange's four-square theorem and an assumed coding with a definability property; the second-incompleteness sentence is obtained only under the hypothesis that the provability formula of T-sharp satisfies D2 and D3, with an informal listing procedure and the Church-Turing thesis in place of a Turing-machine enumeration, and through the cited (unproved) thm:representability. (4) Barwise's p. 43 claim that functions can be defined by recursion in HF(M) because it is admissible is proved only for recursion along the natural numbers (handbook/parts/p02/propositional-languages-valuations-and-truth-functions-w02c-p02-003.tex:268-317); general Sigma-recursion (Makkai A.7 2.16-2.17) is not proved and has no missing-work record.
